podcast.body: During a spirited performance of this song as the last of 10 songs played at their free, unannounced concert in San Francisco, Bono spray-painted the words "rock and roll stops traffic" on a nearby fountain. "Entering the last song of every spirited performance of Pride of the Name of Love, Bono ran over to a nearby fountain and spray painted the words rock and roll stops traffic on it."

podcast.body: U2's biggest hit up to that point, this song was intended to be their third and final song at Live Aid in 1985. However, due to Bono's extended on-stage antics during the previous song, "Bad," the band ran out of time and was unable to perform it. "But the time he was finished, you two's time was up, and they never got to play their third song, which would have been Pride of the Name of Love, their biggest hit to that point."
